Guides › Type checking in CI

Type checking in CI

Pare does not check types. A line like let n: number = "hi" strips without complaint. Type checking is TypeScript's job, and TypeScript 7 ships a native tsc that needs no Node.

Let the build run it

XML 
<PareTypeCheck>true</PareTypeCheck>

Before the strip, the build runs tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json. A type error fails the build.

Get tsc without npm

scripts/get-tsc.cs in the Pare repository fetches the native tsc from the npm registry and checks its sha512, without npm or Node. Copy it into your repo, outside any project directory (a project compiles every .cs below it), and run it on each machine and in CI before the build:

bash 
dotnet run scripts/get-tsc.cs --dest .tools/typescript   # add .tools/ to .gitignore

Tell the build where it is:

XML 
<PropertyGroup>
  <PareTypeCheck>true</PareTypeCheck>
  <PareTscPath>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory).tools/typescript/tsc</PareTscPath>
  <PareTscPath Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOSPlatform('Windows'))">$(PareTscPath).exe</PareTscPath>
</PropertyGroup>
  • The binary is per OS and CPU (@typescript/typescript-<os>-<cpu>: darwin-arm64, win32-x64, linux-x64 and the other arm64/x64 pairs). Fetch it on each machine instead of committing it.
  • Running it again with the same version does nothing. --version <x.y.z> picks another.
  • The script refuses a --dest that is not empty and that it did not fill itself.
  • $(PareTsconfig) defaults to the project's tsconfig.json. It is never copied to the build or publish output.

A tsconfig that matches Pare

JSON 
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "esnext",
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "lib": ["esnext", "dom", "dom.iterable"],
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "erasableSyntaxOnly": true,
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true
  },
  "include": ["wwwroot/js/**/*.ts"]
}

erasableSyntaxOnly makes the editor and tsc flag the same syntax Pare rejects. verbatimModuleSyntax makes you write import type for types, which is what a stripper needs: without type information Pare cannot tell that an imported name is only a type.

Without the build

bash 
pare src --check-only    # syntax Pare cannot erase
tsc --noEmit             # types
